mission.cluster: the checkpoint seam and its bounded fail-closed gate: an unbound port means cannot-verify, and a required checkpoint that fails aborts the restart

portedFiles.src/plugin/checkpoint-gate.ts: checkpoint-gate.mjs (with contracts.mjs carrying the GateResult shape, the failure factory and the unbound port's own constants; the CheckpointOutcome shape and its copy constructor come from the sibling restart-protocol module)

adaptation: TypeScript -> plain ESM JavaScript, Node 24, no new dependencies. `UnboundCheckpointPort` and `CheckpointGate` become factory-built objects; the unbound answer, the fail-closed authorization rule, the throw path and the bounded timeout are carried over path for path.

The donor's single shared contract layer is preserved as a single source. `checkpoint-gate.ts` imports `CheckpointOutcome` and `CheckpointPort` from `../shared/types.js`; that shared layer is the sibling `restart-protocol` module in this same building, and `contracts.mjs` imports `checkpointOutcome` from `../restart-protocol/contracts.mjs` and re-exports it unchanged. The dependency direction is the donor's own (`plugin/* -> shared/*`), expressed as a cross-module import within the building, so there is exactly one declaration of the outcome shape and nothing the gate validates can drift from what the rest of the protocol believes a checkpoint answer is.

`GateResult`, `NO_CHECKPOINT_PORT`, the unbound port's id and reason, and the failure factory stay local, because the donor declares them in `checkpoint-gate.ts` itself and nowhere else. `RestartMode` is the donor's `'application' | 'system'` string, passed straight through to the port and never interpreted.

The donor's `GateResult` interface and its `failure()` helper are exported as `gateResult()` and `checkpointFailure()`: frozen copy-on-construct shapes carrying exactly the donor's fields, so a port cannot smuggle extra state into an audit record.

The donor declared `available` with `this.port instanceof UnboundCheckpointPort`. This port is factory-built, so the unbound port carries a non-exported brand and `isUnboundPort()` checks that brand or the donor's `checkpoint-unbound` id. The check stays exactly as narrow: a port is unavailable only when it is the unbound one.

The donor's `const` failure codes are exported as data: `GATE_FAILURE_REASONS`, `NO_CHECKPOINT_PORT` ('no_checkpoint_port'), `UNBOUND_PORT_ID` ('checkpoint-unbound') and `UNBOUND_PORT_REASON` ('no checkpoint port is bound in this profile').

The timeout is kept ambient and real: `setTimeout` / `clearTimeout` are Node globals, the timer is `unref`'d when the runtime supports it, and the timeout path is tested with a genuine 10 ms budget against a 60 ms port, not with an injected fake timer. The clock used for `elapsedMs` is injected and defaults to a fixed clock pinned at epoch 0 (`createFixedClock()`), so this port never calls `Date.now`.

The donor's inline timeout `Error` becomes `CheckpointTimeoutError`, carrying the donor's message, the port id and the budget. It is still caught by the same `catch` and still becomes `checkpoint_threw` with detail `prepareForRestart threw: checkpoint port <id> did not answer within <timeoutMs> ms`, so no caller-visible behaviour changed.

The donor's `(error as Error).message` assumed the port threw an `Error`. `throwDetail()` keeps `instanceof Error` first and falls back to `String(error)`, so a port that throws a non-Error is still recorded instead of producing `undefined` in the audit detail.
`timeoutMs` defaults to 0 in the factory when it is omitted; the donor required it in its options type. 0 means 'no timeout', which is the donor's own rule, so no new behaviour was introduced.

The donor's `withTimeout` is a module-private helper here and its `T` type parameter is erased; the runtime behaviour, including rejecting a non-Error rejection with `new Error(String(rejection))`, is unchanged.
The donor's `UnboundCheckpointPort` and `CheckpointGate` names are exported as aliases of the factories, so the migration names survive without classes.
knownDifferences: Timers are ambient. `setTimeout` / `clearTimeout` are the one dependency this port does not inject: the donor used them and the task of bounding a hung port needs them. A test drives the real path with a short timeout; `elapsedMs` and every other clock read use the injected `now`, which defaults to a fixed epoch-0 clock instead of `Date.now`.

The donor performed no runtime validation (TypeScript erased it), so a port answering with a missing `detail` would have carried `undefined` and a port answering with `safe: 'yes'` would have authorized a restart in a plain-JavaScript caller. This port validates each answered outcome through the shared `checkpointOutcome()` constructor and throws a `TypeError` at the gate; the thrown error is caught by the donor's own path and becomes `checkpoint_threw`, so a malformed answer cannot authorize a restart either way.

The outcome constructor refuses an incomplete answer: an absent or `undefined` `checkpointId`/`resumeToken` is a missing required field rather than a `null` one, and an empty `reason` or `detail` string is refused rather than accepted. This is a fail-closed restatement of the donor's declared types and not a behaviour the donor performs: the donor has no runtime constructor for `CheckpointOutcome` at all, it is a TypeScript interface that declares `safe`, `reason`, `checkpointId`, `resumeToken`, `completed` and `detail` as required fields, and every donor path that produces one supplies all six with non-empty strings (`failure(reason, detail)` and `UnboundCheckpointPort.prepareForRestart`'s constant literal). No donor-produced value is refused by it, so the strictness cannot reject a legitimate checkpoint answer; it only stops a malformed one from being read as a valid one.

The donor's `withTimeout` left the losing timer running when the port answered first only by clearing it; that is preserved. When `timeoutMs <= 0` the answer is returned unwrapped, so a hung port is waited on forever — the donor's behaviour and the caller's choice, not a new default.

The donor's `CheckpointGate` returned `outcome` unchanged for a required checkpoint and appended ` (checkpoint not required for this request)` only when the checkpoint was not required and the outcome was not safe; neither the suffix nor the required path was softened.

This port never saves task state and never reaches a harness. It calls the bound port and believes only its answer; there is still no default implementation that reports success, and the unbound port still cannot verify anything.

This module no longer declares the outcome shape locally: it is imported from the sibling `restart-protocol` module, which is the port of `src/shared/types.ts`. The donor's `RestartMode` import is replaced by documentation of the string it is; the rest of the protocol and the donor's `restart-executor`, `restart-supervisor` and lock consumers are out of scope.

`createFixedClock()`, `timeoutMessage()`, `throwDetail()`, `isUnboundPort()` and the `CheckpointTimeoutError` class are additions for porting and for the incubator surface; none of them changes an authorization decision.

vectors: the unbound port id is `checkpoint-unbound` and its default reason is exactly `no checkpoint port is bound in this profile`
an unbound port answers {safe:false, reason:'no_checkpoint_port', checkpointId:null, resumeToken:null, completed:false, detail:<reason>} for both restart modes and a custom reason is carried verbatim
acknowledgeResume on an unbound port is false for null, a token and no argument
available is false exactly when the bound port is an unbound one, and true for any other port
a required checkpoint that is safe AND completed is authorized
a required checkpoint with safe:false is not authorized and its detail is kept verbatim with no suffix
a required checkpoint with completed:false is not authorized
a required checkpoint that is neither safe nor completed is not authorized
a checkpoint that is NOT required is always authorized, and the detail suffix ` (checkpoint not required for this request)` appears exactly when the outcome was not safe
a port that throws becomes {safe:false, reason:'checkpoint_threw', ...} with detail `prepareForRestart threw: <message>`, and never authorizes a required request
a rejected promise is the same failure as a throw
a port that throws while acknowledging reports false instead of propagating
a slow port with a 10 ms budget is not authorized, with detail `checkpoint port <id> did not answer within 10 ms`, and a late checkpointId is never carried into the result
timeoutMs <= 0 means no timeout: a 30 ms port answers and still authorizes
elapsedMs is measured from the injected clock, bracketing the port call
the requested mode is what the port is asked about, and the resume token is handed through unchanged
the outcome shape the gate validates is the sibling shared layer's own constructor, so a checkpoint answer is read the same way everywhere in the building

an incomplete outcome is refused (absent required field, or an empty reason/detail) while a complete answer — the unbound port's own literal included — constructs, stays frozen and keeps all six members

PARITY: the unbound port's answer and reason, and acknowledgeResume false
available false exactly for the unbound port
the not-required detail suffix and its exact condition
the bounded timeout message, clearTimeout on answer and unref'd timer
timeoutMs <= 0 meaning no timeout at all
